config.title: KitKatClub Berlin Dress Code - FAQ
config.subtitle: What each night actually asks for, what a ticket does and does not buy, and the phone and consent rules that matter most.

items.q: What is the dress code at KitKatClub Berlin?
items.a: **It depends entirely on which night you go.** The club's general baseline, in its own words, is "NOT your average everyday life clothing", with fetish, sexy, daring, extravagant and original all named as welcome. On top of that, each party publishes its own rule. **Saturday's CarneBall Bizarre** asks for kinky, fetish, gothic, latex and leather, costumes, glitter and glamour or elegant evening wear, and states that **jeans and sports shoes are forbidden**. **Electric Monday** is the relaxed end and accepts smart casual and black T-shirts. **Unity on Thursday** asks you to avoid jeans, T-shirts and sneakers. Read the rule for your specific night before you pack.

items.q: Can I wear jeans or sneakers to KitKatClub?
items.a: **Jeans, essentially never. Sneakers, on exactly one night of the month.** Saturday's listing forbids jeans and sports shoes in writing, Thursday asks you to avoid jeans, T-shirts and sneakers, and Sunday's Nachspiel states no street wear, no jeans and no T-shirts. The exception is **PiepShow on the last Friday of the month**, which lists sporty looks with sportswear and sneakers as a genuine accepted option, while still refusing regular jeans and T-shirts. Electric Monday allows black or colourful T-shirts but bans long-sleeve pullovers.

items.q: Does buying a ticket guarantee I get into KitKatClub?
items.a: **No, and the club says so itself.** Its event listings carry the line "Purchasing a ticket doesn't guarantee entrance. Management reserves the right to refuse entry." Advance tickets are sold by each night's organiser, usually through Resident Advisor, and the club directs all ticket and price questions to that organiser rather than answering them itself. The door is a judgement made by a person on the night, and no outfit, ticket or guest list overrides it.

items.q: What time should I arrive at KitKatClub?
items.a: **Doors open at 20:00 on Friday and Saturday**, which surprises people who plan to arrive at midnight. The club moved to an 8pm weekend opening in spring 2024 and runs a "Come Together" period with chilled music at the pool, specifically so arrivals spread out and the queue gets shorter. The dress code applies from 8pm and so does the usual entry fee, so an early arrival buys a calmer door rather than a cheaper one. Weeknight parties on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday open at 22:00, and Sunday's Nachspiel day rave starts at **08:00 in the morning**.

**No. Treat the whole building as a no-camera space.** Some of the club's own listings state "Strictly NO phones in the club allowed". Where an official photographer works a night, they ask each person first and people who want their outfit photographed opt in, so nobody is photographed for happening to be in frame. The rule exists because the room is full of people who have chosen not to publish how they are dressed or behaving, and one phone pointed at a dancefloor removes that choice from all of them at once.

items.q: What are the consent rules at KitKatClub?
items.a: **Consent is the club's hardest published rule, and the penalty is permanent.** The Saturday listing states plainly that the club is not a swingers club and that touching someone without their agreement, including in passing, leads to a ban for life. Several nights describe themselves as sex-positive, consent-based spaces with play areas in parts of the building. In practice this is simple: you look, you do not touch, and you ask first. No is a complete answer given once. If someone crosses your boundary, the staff are there for exactly that.

items.q: Where is KitKatClub and how do I get home afterwards?
items.a: The club is at **Köpenicker Straße 76, on the corner of Brückenstraße** in Berlin-Mitte. The nearest station is **U Heinrich-Heine-Straße on the U8**, about 190 metres away, with **S+U Jannowitzbrücke** a five-minute walk in the other direction. Getting home depends on the night: after a Friday or Saturday the **U8 runs right through**, roughly every 15 minutes at 04:00, alongside the N60 and N65 buses. After a Monday, Wednesday or Thursday there is no U8 at 03:30 and the first trains are around 04:13, so the **N8 night bus** is the way back. Checked against live departures on 27 August 2026.

items.q: Where can I buy a KitKat outfit in Berlin?
items.a: **Motzstraße in Schöneberg is the fastest place to solve it.** The club publishes its own list of Berlin shops and several of them sit on or beside that street: Mr. B at Motzstraße 22 for leather and rubber, and the Military-Store on the corner of Eisenacher Straße for uniforms, which suit a GEGEN Friday and are specifically refused at Four Play. **Mr. B opens Monday to Friday 12:00 to 20:00, Saturday 11:00 to 20:00, and closes on Sunday**, so shop the day before rather than on the way. You do not need latex: most nights accept a considered look built around one real piece, such as mesh or a harness over dark basics, with boots you can stand in for hours.
